cells.tense: You are sitting with the living thing and letting it grow at its own pace.
cells.ask: Open a window for it: give one growing thing a quiet ten minutes and do nothing but watch. No fixing, no adjusting.
cells.core:
You stay with what you're growing long past the interesting part, and that patience is working on it in ways you won't get to see for a while. You hold back from tweaking, which is rare — most people force growth so it will feel like progress. What comes up under your attention tends to come out sound because you didn't rush it.

The depth underneath all that waiting is real. Stay with something long enough and you stop needing to figure it out and start recognizing it — the same quiet knowing that shows up when you finally admit what you already felt. That isn't laziness and it isn't giving up. It's the part where the growing becomes something you understand.
cells.sheetLine: You grow what you tend by staying, not by pushing.
cells.verb: Going deep into what you are growing until understanding arrives by way of patience rather than thought
cells.place: Where you keep tending something that is still becoming itself

cells.tense: You'll have started transplanting what is growing before it has had time to root.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are growing and say out loud what it needs next, then wait one full day before doing any of it. Let the declaration stand on its own.
cells.core:
You are pulling your growing things toward a version of them you can already see, and the pulling is starting to cost you the plants. There's no cruelty in it — you just want what's coming to arrive now. So you tend harder than the moment calls for. You prune too early, or course-correct before the roots have set. The person you are being with the thing is standing ahead of the thing.

What's underneath is wanting to be sure it turns out. That's care, and it's also driving. Something can hold the structure of what you have and still stay down here with it. You don't have to choose between caring and letting it be, you only have to leave your hands by your side for one more day.

cells.tense: You stood at the edge of the thing and backed away, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Show one thing you are growing to one other person — half-formed, no explanation, no apology. Let them see it in its current state.
cells.core:
You stopped staying with what you were growing, and staying with it is still available to you. You know how to sit through the awkward middle of a thing. But at some point the watching got interrupted, and you haven't gone back to the table since. The plants are still there. The patience is still yours.

What's absent here isn't the ability to go deep. It's the room to do it in. Depth needs to be shared to keep its heat; a private slowness goes cold. More effort pushed into a quiet house won't warm it, and in this case it isn't more work that's called for. It's bringing one small growing thing into contact with someone else, so there's a reason to pick the sitting back up. A person on the other end changes what the watching is for.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what is growing while saying it is simply taking its own course.
cells.ask: Name one choice you made about a growing thing as yours — say 'I picked this' instead of 'it just happened' — about one small decision from this week.
cells.core:
You are tending more carefully than most — the timing, the pace, the amount of space you leave — and you'd say you were only watching. But you choose when to speak and when to stay quiet. You decide what gets noticed and what gets left alone. That choosing runs through every bit of what you do, and you haven't claimed any of it.

It hasn't occurred to you to claim it because it doesn't feel like steering. It feels like holding still. But holding still is a thing you are doing, and it's why things around you come up sound. The recognition you've been giving the plant — this is alive, this is becoming — belongs to you too. Sit with one decision you made and let it be yours.
